title: Awake, My Heart, Arise, My Tongue
description: Awake, My Heart, Arise, My Tongue in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 20, headed “Spiritual apparel; namely, the robe of righteousness, and garments of salvation, Isa. 61. 10”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-wake, my heart, a-rise, my tongue, Pre-pare a tune-ful voice, In God the life of all my joys, A-loud will I re-joice.

lines: Awake, my heart, arise, my tongue,
In God the life of all my joys,
And lest the shadow of a spot
Should on my soul be found,
He took the robe the Saviour wrought,
How far the heavenly robe exceeds
These ornaments, how bright they shine!
The Spirit wrought my faith and love,
But Jesus spent his life to work
Strangely, my soul, art thou array'd

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
